title: certdrift observation
description: What material was looked at, from where, when, and which certificates it contained. Contract version 1. Consumers must tolerate properties and enum-like values they do not know.

contract.description: Contract version. Adding fields keeps 1; renaming, removing or repurposing one requires 2.

format.description: Format of the material. Rejecting unknown formats is deliberate: a consumer that does not understand a format must not read it as X.509.

observation.description: When and from where the material was observed. Descriptive only: it never affects comparison, classification or exit codes.

at.description: Instant of the observation. The only input that derived values depend on.

target.description: Index in certificates[] of the certificate that check and diff operate on.

certificates.description: Every certificate in the material, deduplicated by sha256, in input order.

warnings.description: Facts about the material that the rest of the observation does not show. Always present; empty when there is nothing to report. Ordered as they were found, which follows input order.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 instant in UTC with second precision, e.g. 2026-09-15T14:02:11Z. Certificates only store seconds, so no fraction is ever emitted.

sha256.description: SHA-256 digest as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters, no separators.

cn.description: Common name for quick reading, unescaped. null when the name has no CN component.

dn.description: Full distinguished name in certificate order, components joined with ', '. A comma inside a value keeps its backslash escape (O=Acme\, Inc.), so components stay unambiguous.

index.description: Position of this certificate in certificates[]. Contiguous from 0, after dropping duplicates.

kind.description: Derived from the certificate's own bytes, not its position. Known values: end-entity (basicConstraints does not mark it as a CA), ca. Tolerate unknown values.

selfSigned.description: true when the issuer name equals the subject and the signature verifies with the certificate's own public key. Describes a cryptographic shape; it does NOT mean trusted root.

issuedBy.description: Indices, in ascending order, of the certificates in this material whose subject equals this certificate's issuer and whose public key verifies its signature. Empty when the issuer is not in the material. A self-signed certificate includes itself. A cross-signed CA in the material produces more than one entry.

serial.description: Serial number in uppercase hexadecimal, no separators or prefix, as Node.js reports it. A leading '-' marks a negative serial, which non-conforming certificates can carry.

eku.description: Extended Key Usage: known names (serverAuth, clientAuth, codeSigning, emailProtection, timeStamping, OCSPSigning) or the OID as text, sorted. null when the extension is absent, which means EKU does not restrict the purpose — not that the certificate is good for everything.

spkiSha256.description: Fingerprint of the public key (SubjectPublicKeyInfo, DER). Identifies the key regardless of the certificate that carries it.

san.description: Subject Alternative Names by type. The four lists are always present, possibly empty. Other types (DirName, othername, …) are not represented here and produce a SAN_TYPE_UNREPRESENTED warning.

ip.description: Canonical form (IPv6 compressed and lowercase), sorted.

algorithm.description: Node.js key type identifier in lowercase. Known values: rsa, rsa-pss, dsa, ec, ed25519, ed448, ml-dsa-44, ml-dsa-65, ml-dsa-87. Tolerate unknown values. null when Node.js does not identify the key type.

size.description: Size in bits: modulus length for RSA, curve size for P-256/P-384/P-521. null when the algorithm has no equivalent size (Ed25519, ML-DSA) or the curve is not in the name map.

curve.description: For EC keys, the NIST name (P-256, P-384, P-521) when one exists, otherwise the name Node.js reports (e.g. brainpoolP256r1). null for non-EC keys.

derived.description: Values computed from observation.at. Ignored by diff. Checks evaluate the original dates, never these rounded values.

daysRemaining.description: (notAfter - at) in days, one decimal. Negative once expired.

lifetimeFraction.description: (at - notBefore) / (notAfter - notBefore), two decimals. Above 1 once expired, negative while not yet valid. null when notAfter is not after notBefore, since the validity period has no duration.

source.description: Where the material came from. Known kinds: file, stdin and host (produced by the CLI); external and bytes (produced only through the library). Tolerate unknown kinds.

ref.description: Text shown to a human to identify the source: a path, '-' for stdin, host:port, or free text for external sources.

servername.description: Server name sent in the TLS handshake (SNI). Only for host; null when none was sent.

provider.description: Optional label of an external source, e.g. vault. Metadata only.

code.description: Stable code for programs. Known values: DUPLICATE_CERTIFICATE, SAN_TYPE_UNREPRESENTED. Tolerate unknown values.

certificate.description: index of the certificate the warning is about, or null when it concerns no single certificate. For a dropped duplicate, the index of the occurrence that was kept.

message.description: Human-readable English text. Never parse it; decide with code.
